title: 20.2 A 67μW/Channel, 0.13nW/Synapse/b Nose-on-a-Chip for Noninvasive Diagnosis of Diseases with On-Chip Incremental Learning
problem: Portable electronic noses (E-noses) for disease diagnosis via exhaled gas analysis face accuracy drift across environments and patients; high power consumption limits battery-operated portability. Traditional centralized ML preprocessing requires continuous external computation and doesn't adapt to patient-specific signatures.
motivation: Early disease detection via non-invasive breath analysis reduces patient discomfort and enables at-home diagnostics; on-chip incremental learning adapts to environment/patient variation without frequent recalibration.
method: The system uses a low-power electronic nose front-end (67 microwatts per channel) with gas sensors and analog signal conditioning (preparing the raw sensor signals for processing). Instead of sending data to a cloud server for analysis, a lightweight neural network runs directly on the chip and learns from each patient's individual breath signature in real time, using just 0.13 nanowatts per synapse (neural connection) per bit. This on-chip learning allows the sensor to automatically calibrate itself and adapt to each specific patient without needing external connectivity.
key_novelty: The system uses on-chip incremental learning—where the neural network continuously learns and adapts—to calibrate itself specifically for each patient using only 0.13 nanowatts per synapse per bit, which lets it maintain accuracy even as environments change.
contributions: Ultra-low-power E-nose front-end: 67 μW per channel including sensor interface
On-chip incremental learning reduces external computation dependency
0.13 nW/synapse/b synaptic power enables real-time adaptation on battery power
Patient-specific signatures improve disease detection accuracy across locations
baselines: Conventional E-nose systems with centralized ML
limitations: Classification accuracy, number of learned diseases, and online learning convergence rate not specified.
primary_theme: Portable E-nose with on-chip learning for health diagnosis
